messages:
carlos (eng-platform): heads-up — followup from the rate/abuse RFC: we need a concrete handoff contract between the admission rate-limiter and the abuse-detector. quick sync?
ben (eng-infra): +1. want to avoid circular dependencies and double-charging quotas.
alice (eng-security): goal: let admission make fast allow/soft-shed decisions while abuse-detector flags longer-term penalties. keep it async where possible.
diana (eng-runtime): runtime prefers a small sync response (<=1ms added) with an opinionated enum: ALLOW / SOFT_DECAY / REJECT. then async events for heavier analysis.
carlos (eng-platform): sketch of minimal sync payload I had in mind: request_id, tenant_id, token_cost_estimate, short client signals (ip_hash, user_agent_hash). that's it. heavy telemetry separate.
ben (eng-infra): that sounds sensible. one pain point: quota accounting — if we soft-shed, do we still count token consumption against quota? tradeoff.
eve (product): product POV: predictable billing is important for customers. soft-shed should be transparent and ideally not charged as full quota. can we expose a metric? :eyes:
alice (eng-security): prefer this rule: soft-shed => charge 50% or configurable mapping per tenant. prevents griefing and keeps incentives.
diana (eng-runtime): implementation note: runtime will accept an AdmissionResponse that includes: action (ALLOW/SHED/REJECT), charge_multiplier (float string), override_ttl. e.g.:
```
AdmissionResponse {
  action: "SOFT_SHED",
  charge_multiplier: "0.5",
  penalty_score: "0.72",
  mitigation_tag: "rate-limited-abuse-v2"
}
```
ben (eng-infra): storing penalty_score on central ledger allows coordinated backoff across regions. but watch out for hot writes. maybe keep ephemeral cache + eventual consistency.
carlos (eng-platform): also need an idempotent way to re-evaluate after model-fallback. should admission include model_variant hint so abuse-detector can reason about cost/risk?
alice (eng-security): yes include model_variant string. but redact PII — do not send full prompts. only hashed prefixes.
eve (product): how do customers see this? we should expose an explanation field for transparency in logs (not user-facing).
diana (eng-runtime): ok for sync path we keep explanation short (error code or tag). full explanation available via async fetch by SRE/owner.
ben (eng-infra): scaling: we should allow local fallbacks when central abuse-detector is unreachable. default policy: ALLOW with charge_multiplier=1 and mark for later audit. fallback behavior must be config-driven per environment.
carlos (eng-platform): +1. record: fallback_policy ENUM {LOCAL_ALLOW, LOCAL_SHED, LOCAL_REJECT, FAIL_OPEN_WITH_AUDIT}. default LOCAL_ALLOW in edge, stricter in private deployments.
alice (eng-security): one more: define abuse_signal taxonomy v1 (rapid-retry, skewed prompt patterns, token-entropy anomalies). make it extensible.
carlos (eng-platform): i'll open a short RFC PR with the AdmissionResponse proto + example flows (canary, fallback, billing mapping). tagging eng-security + infra.
eve (product): thanks — please include customer-facing FAQ draft for soft-shed behavior.
infra-bot: deploy-check: admission-proto v1 lint OK (no blockers)
ben (eng-infra): followup task list: 1) proto + schema 2) cache/ledger design 3) fallback configs per deployment 4) billing mapping doc. I'll spin up stubs.
carlos (eng-platform): perfect. meeting next thursday 11am to finalize mappings. :calendar:
